beats.trigger: ## Multi-Agent Systems
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Hire three agents to search. Three more to decide. The filesystem is the meeting room.
beats.got: Something about six agents and files. No idea what it costs or what I get.

beats.trigger: [Schedule your personal agent](exercises/personal-agent-homework.md) to read your challenge memory for a week.
beats.got: Homework I did not know about. Nobody told me there was prework.

beats.trigger: **Analyze** handoff failures: hidden conflicts, clashing dialects, beige averaging
beats.got: Verbs and jargon. No outcome I can put in a board paper.

beats.trigger: Three agents search Confluence, OneDrive and practitioner articles, and three more decide what it means.
beats.got: Six agents will read our internal documents. IT has not approved that for finance data.

beats.trigger: The agent writes the message first and sends only after approval.
beats.got: Someone named a risk and a human approval gate before I had to ask. That is the first thing today I would accept.

beats.trigger: Richard Rumelt's term for the one thing that, if solved, releases pressure on everything else.
beats.got: A consultant's term for my main problem. I am not sure I want an agent telling me what it is. The 'call you'd stay late to make' wording is soft.

beats.trigger: **Time:** ~28 minutes.
beats.got: Four sessions open at once, pasting prompts, no cost and no result I can check. Not my spreadsheet either.

beats.trigger: You can't yet tell if the answer is right. That is expected.
beats.got: I spent 22 minutes on an answer nobody can verify yet. That is exactly what I dislike about AI programmes.

beats.trigger: When do you split, and how?
beats.got: A question about splitting agents. At least it is a question, not a claim.

beats.trigger: A hundred tiny agents cost more to coordinate than they save.
beats.got: Agents have a coordination cost, so cost is at least acknowledged. No figure, though.

beats.trigger: If one agent can produce what you need, use one.
beats.got: The default is the cheap option. A sensible rule, and the opposite of hype.

beats.trigger: A legal-policy agent shouldn't have customer-data access.
beats.got: Three tests for splitting, and access control is one of them. I can map that to our own segregation of duties.

beats.trigger: Split for a reason, not because "three is more thorough".
beats.got: The course itself warns against buying more than you need. That earns some credibility.

beats.trigger: The synthesizer then commits to one diagnosis and drops what does not serve it.
beats.got: It picks one view and drops the rest. Fine, but dropping things silently is a control risk.

beats.trigger: Could one prompt produce the same quality of output?
beats.got: A test I can apply to any vendor pitch.

beats.trigger: **Helper agents in one session (the Phase 2 move).**
beats.got: Two ways of building it, with names I do not follow. This is for the IT people.

beats.trigger: One agent can call another for a different stance, source zone, or working style.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: A retriever finds two numbers and the curator keeps one.
beats.got: The failure is a number silently dropped between steps. That is my audit risk exactly.

beats.trigger: If one well-prompted agent does the job, write that prompt.
beats.got: Repeats the earlier point, but I agree with it.

beats.trigger: confident right before a failed handoff.
beats.got: Agents can be confidently wrong. I assumed so.

beats.trigger: Prompt your stuck system to diagnose whether the bug lives in the sources, the processing, or the boundary between agents.
beats.got: Sources, processing, boundary. Roughly input, calculation, control.

beats.trigger: move the risky step from "do" to "propose."
beats.got: Risky steps become proposals that a human approves. I know that as a four-eyes principle.

beats.trigger: Five minutes. The agent reviews the four prompts, the retrieval files, the synthesizer's briefing and the conversation, then rewrites CLAUDE.md in place and reports what changed.
beats.got: The agent rewrites its own instructions file. Who signs that off?

beats.trigger: The audit reads how your agents handed work to each other. It does not check whether the briefing is true.
beats.got: The course states plainly that nothing here verifies the result. I wanted that said, and it was said before I asked.

beats.trigger: Push back where the summary is wrong
beats.got: I have to challenge the output myself. That takes time, and time costs money.

beats.trigger: The synthesized briefing's correctness stays an open question today.
beats.got: After 50 minutes I leave without knowing if the answer is right. I cannot take that to the board.

beats.trigger: **Optional move: pressure-test the memory.**
beats.got: Optional homework. I will skip it.

beats.trigger: Split only where agents can't be one: access, dialect, stance.
beats.got: One rule: default to one agent, split only for access, dialect or stance. I can use that.

beats.trigger: [Agent Trigger List, After Module 3]
beats.got: More reading links.

beats.trigger: Agents add non-deterministic behaviour, prompt injection (direct, or inside retrieved text) and emergent capability you can only bound.
beats.got: Agent risk sits on top of normal security, and the reading names the risks. This is what I would take to IT.

beats.trigger: An agent that works across connected systems has access to those systems.
beats.got: The worst-case-access question is a finance question. This is the first heading framed as risk.

beats.trigger: add an agent for a critical dependency, or a plan visualisation.
beats.got: Vague homework with no stated payoff.

take_homes: Default to one agent. Only split for different access, dialect or stance. Anyone selling me six agents has to pass that test.
The risky step should be a proposal a human approves. That is the demo's Slack gate, and I can ask IT for it.
The course says nothing checks whether the answer is true. I will ask who verifies the output before anyone trusts it.

monday.move: Ask my controller to try the month-end variance commentary with a single agent, no splitting, output as a draft for her to approve.
monday.stop_condition: Stop if it takes longer than doing it by hand, or if one number differs from the ledger.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: I saw no price, no usage cost and no payback. Nothing showed that this is a capability my organisation builds. It still looks like tools I would license, only with more steps.

one_line: The don't-split rule and the admission that nothing checks the answer are good, but I spent 50 minutes and left with no number and no verified result.
